chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no divorce before marriage, and no emancipation before ownership.'

key_terms.طَلَاق: Talaq — the Islamic form of divorce, a unilateral declaration by the husband dissolving a valid marriage contract
key_terms.عِتْق: Itq — the manumission or emancipation of a slave, a legally recognized act in classical Islamic law
key_terms.مِلْك: Milk — ownership or possession; specifically the ownership of a slave, prerequisite for the validity of emancipation
key_terms.نِكَاح: Nikah — the Islamic marriage contract; prerequisite for the validity of talaq

ai.seo_question: Is divorce valid before marriage in Islam according to hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a prophetic ruling establishing two fundamental legal principles: that a man cannot divorce a woman he has not yet married, and that he cannot free a slave he does not yet own. This hadith was narrated in the context of pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabian society where some individuals would issue divorce or manumission declarations prospectively, and the Prophet prohibited such legally void declarations. The ruling reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle that legal acts require their prerequisite conditions to be already fulfilled.
